issues.title: [CUDA 13.2] Inductor training accuracy regression for BertForMaskedLM (HF benchmark) vs CUDA 13.0
issues.author: atalman
issues.body:
### Summary

On the new CUDA 13.2 inductor CI lane, the `inductor_huggingface` **training** accuracy check regresses for **`BertForMaskedLM`**, while the same model/suite passes on the existing CUDA 13.0 lane (same A10G / sm86 runner, same commit).

`check_accuracy.py` verdict on cu13.2:
```
Error: 1 models have accuracy status regressed:
    BertForMaskedLM
```

### Details

The failing comparison is the model's **scalar training loss** (`shape=torch.Size([])`, `numel=1`), so the fp64 RMSE ratio is noise-dominated:

```
RMSE (res-fp64): 0.10322, (ref-fp64): 0.03272, shape=torch.Size([]),
res.dtype: torch.float32, multiplier: 3.000000, tol: 0.010000
```

The accuracy gate is `res_error <= multiplier * ref_error + tol/10`:
- cu13.2: `0.10322 <= 3.0 * 0.03272 + 0.001 = 0.09916` → **FAIL** (over by ~0.004)
- cu13.0: same model → **PASS** (res_error is below the 3x threshold)

So `res_error` (compiled-vs-fp64) is ~3.15x the eager `ref_error` (eager-vs-fp64) on CUDA 13.2 but within 3x on CUDA 13.0. For a scalar loss this is close to noise, but it is a reproducible cu13.2-vs-cu13.0 delta — most likely a cuBLAS/cuSOLVER numeric change in the 13.2 toolkit.

### Evidence

- Failing (cu13.2): https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/30049239912/job/89362543600
- Passing (cu13.0, same suite/runner, `main`): https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/30057644058/job/89375694344
- The 5 `eager_fail_to_run` models (Blenderbot, Qwen3-0.6B, gemma-2-2b, Llama-3.2-1B, whisper-tiny) are A10G OOMs and are **expected/tolerated on both lanes** — they are not the regression.

### Workaround (already applied to unblock the cu13.2 lane)

`BertForMaskedLM` was added to `use_larger_multiplier_for_smaller_tensor` in `benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py` (as already done for `GPT2ForSequenceClassification`), granting a 10x multiplier for the scalar output (threshold → 0.3282), which passes on cu13.2 and does not affect cu13.0 (already passes at the stricter 3x). Landed in #190948.

**This issue tracks the underlying numeric divergence**, which the tolerance bump masks. If the cu13.2 delta is confirmed benign (scalar-loss noise), this can be closed; if `res_error` grows further or appears on larger-tensor outputs, it should be root-caused in the 13.2 math libraries.

### Environment

- CUDA 13.2 (vs 13.0 baseline), inductor, training, `inductor_huggingface` suite
- Runner: `mt-l-x86aavx2-29-113-a10g` (A10G, sm86), float32
- Model: `BertForMaskedLM`

### Repro

```
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py --accuracy --training --backend inductor \
  --device cuda --only BertForMaskedLM
```

issues.title: [RFC] Inductor / AOTI tests: decouple “correct codegen path” from tight eager-fp16 equality
issues.author: iupaikov-amd
issues.body:
## 1. Summary

- Many Inductor and AOTI tests **prove two things at once**: (a) the **compiled path** matches the scenario we care about, and (b) **eager fp16** matches **compiled fp16** to a very tight tolerance. Those goals are often unrelated.
- When eager/compiled check fails on one vendor or SKU while the logic path is fine, we get **noise in CI and review**: skips, tolerance PRs, and repeated explanation - without strengthening the signal for the original regression.
- **fp16** is usually a **red herring**: the interesting question is often **routing, grid, or reference choice**, not “bit-identical GEMM across every math backend.”
- **Dedicated suites already cover fp16 matmul accuracy** (OpInfo, matmul tests). Re-encoding the same bar in **narrow integration tests** duplicates work and **varies by architecture** (e.g. different reduction tiling across GPUs).
- **Ask:** treat this as an incremental cleanup opportunity — tests that were reasonable when written can be upgraded to match the failure mode (structure, reference dtype, or codegen hints) while staying **vendor-neutral**.

---

## 2. Example: `test_bmm_large_batch_dynamic` (AOTI BMM, large dynamic batch)

- PR [#178617](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/178617) introduced logic: **dynamic** batch BMM with **`B > 65535`** must **launch legally** and **index batches correctly** (Triton batch split across `grid_y` / `grid_z`). This logic is checked by comparing if eager vs compiled outputs are bitwise identical. While this in theory covers the regression, it also is prone to 1 ULP fp16 jitter due to reordering on different archs. 
- [#183630](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/183630) scaled inputs to reduce benign fp16 noise for CUDA, which is essentially a tolerance increase in disguise. This makes the test less flaky for **some** archs, but doesn't solve the root of the issue.
- Tight **`same()`** / eager-fp16 equality is **stricter than the bug** needs and **varies by hardware** (e.g. [#179958](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/179958), [#184531](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/184531)) — **false failures** even when the **grid fix** is sound.

---

## 3. Other examples (same pattern family)

| Link | Note |
|------|------|
| [#183630](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/183630) | `test_bmm_large_batch_dynamic` — input scaling / tolerance / CUDA follow-up |
| [#184531](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/184531) | `test_bmm_large_batch_dynamic` — tolerance / ROCm follow-up |
| [#182028](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/182028) | ROCm MI200 — flex vs SDPA `assert_close` tolerances |
| [#186889](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/186889) | XPU — relaxed `assertEqual` vs eager (atomic ordering) |
| [#169694](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/169694) | Transformer tests — **golden** precision / reference choice |
| [#183691](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/183691) | Test infra — tolerance overrides (helps **symptoms**; root cause is still design in individual tests) |

---

## 4. Conclusion & proposed next steps

- We would like to advocate for having some sort of test design guidelines to avoid such problems in the future and help to redesign some of the existing tests. Since this problem is universal for all vendors and multitude of archs we would like to bring this to your attention. As Inductor and hardware diversity grow, **narrowing the logic** per test is a good way to move forward.
- **Proposals (pick per test):**
  - **Match logic to risk:** grid / launch bugs → **shape, finiteness, boundary indices**, optional **codegen / log substring**; fp16 GEMM agreement → **leave to OpInfo / matmul** suites or use **FP32 reference + documented tol**.
  - **Tier or split checks:** small-shape **strict** + large-shape **reference-based**, so one failure mode doesn’t block the other.
  - **Document intent in-test** (one comment): what regression file / PR motivated the scenario—helps future edits stay aligned.
- **Proposed direction:** **FP32 matmul reference** (or similar), **boundary row checks** around **65535**, optional **Inductor log / codegen hints** for the batch reconstruction — **same regression intent**, **less coupling** to eager fp16 BLAS. I will link a draft PR to highlight what was described.

issues.title: [ROCm] torch 2.13 wheel: "Can't detect vectorized ISA for CPU" in torch.compile smoke test on non-ROCm image (regression vs 2.12.1)
issues.author: atalman
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2` wheel fails the `torch.compile` smoke test with
`RuntimeError: Can't detect vectorized ISA for CPU` when it is imported/run on
a **non-ROCm** image (e.g. `pytorch/almalinux-builder:cpu-main`), where
`torch.cuda.is_available()` is `False` and the compile check exercises the
CPU / Inductor path.

This looks like a regression:

- ✅ `torch==2.12.1+rocm7.2` runs the **same** smoke test on the same
  environment and succeeds — it prints `Picked CPU ISA VecAVX2 bit width 256`.
- ✅ `torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2` succeeds when run on the **ROCm** builder image
  (`pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:rocm7.2`).
- ❌ `torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2` fails on a non-ROCm image.

So the 2.13 ROCm wheel appears to depend on something present in the ROCm
builder image to detect the CPU vectorized ISA, whereas 2.12.1 did not.

### Repro

```bash
# In a plain (non-ROCm) manylinux/almalinux CPU image:
pip install torch==2.13.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/test/rocm7.2
cd .ci/pytorch
python smoke_test.py --package torchonly
```

(`pick_vec_isa()` / `valid_vec_isa_list()`) is returning an empty list on the
